scenes.question: What if the record has more than one step?

beats.say: Imagine a long road with several speed bumps. Feeling for the single biggest bump is easy. But to drive safely, you want a map of every bump along the way.

Instruments joined the fire record at several moments: Aqua in 2002, S-NPP in 2012, NOAA-20 in 2018, NOAA-21 in 2023. Formula thirty-four, PELT, finds every step in a series at once, with a penalty declared in advance, so it cannot be tuned to tell a story.

scenes.title: More than one seam
scenes.subtitle: October + November fire cell-days · Punjab and Haryana · FIREWORK archive calendar

beats.say: Here is the raw stitched record again, starting in 2001. Look at the very first bar: it is far lower, because only Terra was flying. Aqua joined in 2002.
Then comes the big step at 2012, when VIIRS takes over. So the raw record has at least two instrument steps, and PELT should find both.

parts.say: We search over every possible set of break points, tau one to tau K, and pick the best one.
Best means the smallest total cost. The breaks cut the series into segments, and each segment pays a cost, C, for how badly a flat level fits it.

But every extra break also pays a penalty, beta. Without it, we could cut the series everywhere and get a perfect fit. The penalty is set before looking at the answer, from the noise level and the length of the series.
The cost of a segment is the sum of squared distances of each month from that segment's average. A segment with a single steady level costs little.

steps.label: Monthly values
steps.say: PELT runs on 299 monthly values, logged and with each calendar month's median removed, so the burning seasons themselves do not count as steps.

steps.label: Minimum segment
steps.say: Each segment must last at least 12 months. On the raw stitched series, PELT finds 2 breaks: March 2002 and October 2011.

steps.label: Breaks after harmonising
steps.say: On the harmonised series, only 1 break is left, in March 2002. The 2011 to 2012 break, VIIRS joining, is gone. The 2002 break remains because it is Aqua joining Terra, a step inside MODIS that the MODIS-to-VIIRS calibration does not touch.

scenes.title: All the steps in the record

beats.say: This figure shows the deseasonalised log monthly fire cell-days, with the change points found by PELT in red. The top panel is the raw stitched series, with two breaks.
The bottom panel is the harmonised series. The VIIRS seam has vanished, and only the early Aqua step remains.

beats.label: The formula, numbered F34
beats.say: On the FIREWORK website, this method lives in the Formulas section. Its page shows the equation, numbered as formula 34, with every symbol explained.

beats.label: Where it comes from · why · how · example
beats.say: Below it, four short cards explain where the method comes from, why FIREWORK needs it, how it works step by step, and a worked example. The full derivation is in the PDF on the same page.

points: Minimise segment cost + penalty per break
Harmonised: only 2002-03 left, the Aqua step inside MODIS

beats.say: So, to remember: PELT finds every step at once, with a penalty fixed in advance. Harmonisation removes the VIIRS seam, and the remaining Aqua step is reported, not hidden.
